newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, Swiss cuts losses.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, Swiss cuts losses.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended sporadic pit trading mixed.

Sterling cut its big morning gains during an afternoon pullback that floor brokers traced to talks between British Telecommunications and MCI Communications about a "business combination." A source close to the deal said BT aimed to increase its current 20 percent stake in MCI to 100 percent.
"It was the deal with MCI and Telecom," said one floor broker. They said such a deal would entail selling sterling for U.S. dollars.
"They would need to purchase dollars," said another.
But big fund buying near the close, which continued in the post-close minutes, popped the British currency back up again, they said.
The fund tried to buy 1,000 December sterling at the close and only got some 600 executed at a price of about 1.6340, so it continued bidding in the post-close session, they said.
Brokers estimated the fund, which often is seen in the Japanese yen, bought about 1,600 nearby sterling on the day.
The Swiss franc also moved upward during the afternoon after posting steep morning losses and closed barely changed.
Brokers tied recovery in Swiss franc futures to crosses and options-related hedge buying.
The December Swiss franc during the morning had skidded to a new contract low as it breached key support near the $0.7876 level, roughly 1.2750 spot.
It nearly touched a cash target of 1.2800, or about $0.7847 in nearby futures, before bouncing back up.
But the Swiss currency's weak fundamental and technical position left some chartists looking for more downside soon.
The yen's bounce stemmed partly from afternoon comments by former U.S. Treasury secretary Lloyd Bentsen.
